newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: NEW PLANS MOOTED FOR FOKKER RELAUNCH.
newsitem.headline: NEW PLANS MOOTED FOR FOKKER RELAUNCH.

text.p: Bankrupt Dutch planemaker Fokker, considered doomed after an apparently final rescue package was abandoned in December, may yet fly again if new talks currently underway are successful.
Dutch industrial group Stork confirmed on Thursday it was part of ongoing discussions over Fokker's future.
"We are involved in negotiations over a possible relaunch," a Stork spokesman said.
Stork bought Fokker's profitable maintenance and aircraft component operations last year.
Stork confirmed the discussions also involved the president of Dutch industrial group Begemann, Andre Deleye, who Dutch media say is the driving force behind the rescue bid.
"There are negotiations between Stork and Mr Deleye," the spokesman said. "He has taken the initiative, while we are more on the sidelines."

Dutch daily Algemeen Dagblad reported on Thursday that the discussions, which also involved a large Singapore finance company, had reached a critical stage, with the Dutch government closely involved.
The Dutch Ministry of Economic Affairs refused to comment.
Stork said in October last year it would be prepared to take a minority stake in a re-started Fokker.

Its purchase of the maintenance and components businesses was conditional on the division being sold back should Stork prove unwilling or unable to cooperate with a future buyer of the planemaking activities.
"When Stork finds out if the plans are good, we will want to take a percentage when there is a restart," the spokesman said.

Fokker was declared bankrupt in March last year and looked to have finally gone to the wall in December, when its principal suitor, Korea's Samsung Aerospace, pulled out of protracted negotiations over a rescue bid.
One of its key suppliers, Shorts, a unit of Canada's Bombardier Group, had decided in November to close down production of wings for the Fokker F-70 and F-100 regional jets.
But Algemeen Dagblad said Delaye had reached agreement with Shorts to resume production and had landed pre-orders for 35 new aircraft.
The project has lined up initial capital of around 400 million guilders, the paper said.

Fokker shares, which are no longer officially listed but are still traded, were up 37 percent to 0.89 guilders at the midsession in Amsterdam. -- Amsterdam newsroom +31 20 504 5000, Fax +31 20 504 5040
